task.historical_context: Throughout United States history, many constitutional and civic issues have been debated by Americans. These debates have resulted in efforts by individuals, groups, and governments to address these issues. These efforts have achieved varying degrees of success. One of these constitutional and civic issues is Prohibition.
requirements: Describe the historical circumstances surrounding this constitutional or civic issue
Explain efforts by individuals, groups, and/or governments to address this constitutional or civic issue
Discuss the impact of the efforts on the United States and/or on American society
guidelines: Develop all aspects of the task
Explain at least two efforts to address the issue
Incorporate information from at least four documents
Support the theme with relevant facts, examples, and details
Use a logical and clear plan of organization, including an introduction and a conclusion that are beyond a restatement of the theme

definitions.describe: to illustrate something in words or tell about it
definitions.explain: to make plain or understandable; to give reasons for or causes of; to show the logical development or relationships of
definitions.discuss: to make observations about something using facts, reasoning, and argument; to present in some detail

dimensions.label: Task Identification
dimensions.student_prompt: Find where the essay addresses each of the three parts of the task: historical circumstances, efforts to address the issue, and impact. Identifying the topic sentence — or any sentence in that section — is enough.
dimensions.description: Does the essay address all three parts of the task: historical circumstances, efforts, and impact?

dimensions.label: Document Use
dimensions.student_prompt: Find sentences where the essay uses information from the source documents — look for "Document 1", direct quotes, or a clear paraphrase of a source. Check the side panel to verify.
dimensions.description: Does the essay incorporate relevant information from the source documents? How many documents are used?
dimensions.tip: Why this matters: the task requires using at least four documents. An essay can sound smart and be totally accurate, yet still score low if it never cites the documents. As you compare essays, notice which ones point to Docs 1–6 — and which don't.

dimensions.label: Supporting Details
dimensions.student_prompt: Find sentences that include specific facts, examples, statistics, names, dates, or other concrete details that support the essay's claims.
dimensions.description: Does the essay include specific facts, examples, and details — or is it vague and general?

dimensions.label: Analysis vs. Description
dimensions.student_prompt: Find sentences that ANALYZE (explain why, evaluate, draw conclusions) rather than just DESCRIBE (state facts without interpretation).
dimensions.description: Does the essay analyze, evaluate, and draw conclusions — or does it just retell facts?

dimensions.label: Outside Information
dimensions.student_prompt: Find sentences that include relevant historical knowledge NOT found in any of the 6 source documents.
dimensions.description: Does the essay bring in relevant knowledge beyond what the documents provide?

dimensions.label: Organization
dimensions.student_prompt: Find the introduction, the conclusion, and the topic sentence that opens each body section. Does each section start with a simple sentence that says what it's about?
dimensions.description: Does the essay have a logical plan, a real introduction, and a meaningful conclusion?
dimensions.tip: Why this matters: strong essays open each section with a simple topic sentence — "One effort to address Prohibition was..." — and start a new paragraph for each part of the task. Notice which essays signpost their sections clearly, and which run everything together.

dimensions.label: Inaccuracies
dimensions.student_prompt: Find sentences that contain historical errors, misattributions, or factual mistakes. Check claims against the source documents and your own knowledge.
dimensions.description: Does the essay contain factual errors? This is an advanced skill — can you spot what the writer got wrong?
